description: The Financial Access Survey is the International Monetary Fund's annual supply-side dataset on access to and use of financial services, compiled by the IMF Statistics Department from national central banks and regulators. The dataset page read on 2026-09-28 describes annual statistics on financial service access and usage, with selected series broken down by gender, by type of provider (commercial banks, credit unions, microfinance institutions and others) and by customer type (households and small and medium enterprises); the survey covers indicators such as branches, automated teller machines, agents, accounts, deposits, loans and mobile money, reported per country as a time series. Coverage is global by country, annually, with the 2025 results released on 29 October together with an annual report on fintech. Access is free through the IMF data portal with a viewer, bulk download and an API. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): IMF copyright and terms of use (not readable from the cloud on 2026-09-29; the dataset page does not restate them). Caveats: figures are national aggregates reported by authorities, without locations of access points, and coverage varies between countries and years. It serves resilience and capacity planning analysis of financial service infrastructure, for example the density of branches and ATMs as payment access points. Related record: data-kenya-finaccess-geospatial-mapping-2015 gives point locations of financial access points for one country.
